decisive_finding.cause: Termination, escalation, and absence proof track only the direct child's original process group while the Darwin sandbox policy allows process operations. A descendant can call setsid(), detach its standard streams, ignore SIGTERM, and leave that group.
decisive_finding.independent_probe: The real adapter returned in 198 ms with the original group absent while the detached descendant remained alive.
decisive_finding.impact: Process-group absence does not prove descendant absence; wall-time and resource-confinement behavior can return success while work continues outside the tracked group.

required_correction: Add the actual-adapter setsid descendant regression and require it to fail before the correction and pass afterward without reviewer cleanup.
Enforce containment beyond mutable process-group membership, or enforceably prohibit session/process-group escape on the supported host; do not infer descendant absence from original group absence.
Prove multiple descendants, rapid reparenting, direct-child early exit, ignored SIGTERM, interrupt, output limit, wall timeout, and already-exited cases leave no live process.
Preserve network, filesystem, CPU, file-size, address-space, backend-integrity, policy-digest, collision, recovery, and supplied-outcome controls; keep Darwin RLIMIT_DATA explicitly unclaimed.
Do not broaden supported fixture behavior merely to retain tests; state any enforceable child-process restriction as product behavior and verify it through the real adapter.
claim_ceiling: No fixture resource-confinement acceptance, public HCT-FIXTURES integration, routine/strict journey, readiness, release, node closure, or completion.
no_claim_statement: This decision does not claim fixture confinement, public integration, readiness, release, node closure, or goal completion.
